buttonLabel: "Explore the history of Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama"
lead: >-
  Travelling through Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama reveals different periods
  of Central American history. At Copán, see a Maya civilisation's chronicle
  carved in stone; in León and Granada, the legacy of Spanish colonial cities;
  and in Panama, colonial streets, the canal and the living traditions of
  the Emberá people. Ada Tours includes these countries in longer journeys
  through six or eight countries. We explain the actual stops, differences
  between itineraries and time needed to appreciate their history.
---

## Three countries and three different historical themes

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with main stops in Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama and the "Culture and History" interest. Both journeys cover **more than three countries**, so choose according to the days you want to experience rather than assuming that the combination in the catalogue address denotes a separate trip restricted to these three.

[Honduras](/honduras/) is represented above all by ancient [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), a centre of Classic Maya culture. [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/) introduces the Spanish colonial cities of [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/) and [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), their cathedrals and urban traditions. [Panama](/panama/) completes the historical story with [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/), the [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) and a visit to an Emberá community in the [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) area.

The combination provides three distinct perspectives. How did the Maya live and record their history? How did Central America's colonial cities develop? How did trade, sea routes and Indigenous peoples shape modern Panama? Each question has specific sites in the programmes.

## Honduras: Copán's stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway

Both itineraries reach the ruins of [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). Its stone stelae and reliefs display Maya sculptors' skill, while the Hieroglyphic Stairway sheds light on how rulers preserved dynastic memory. Careful examination of the carvings and inscriptions is essential to understanding the site; its temples add context but do not replace that experience.

On the [26-day tour through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), the ruins are visited on day 13 before the group proceeds to El Salvador. On the [24-day “Best of Central America” journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/), the excursion also precedes the transfer to San Salvador. Honduras therefore functions primarily as **an archaeological stop**, rather than a multi-day overview of its regions.

If Copán is the main purpose of your journey, compare [culture and history tours involving Honduras](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/honduras/). On a long trip, leave enough time both for the monument and for the drive after the excursion so that neither part of the day is rushed.

## Nicaragua: two colonial cities and Estelí's contemporary culture

In [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), travellers explore historic districts, squares and religious architecture. In [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/), the main themes are the cathedral, local art and urban history. Both developed during the colonial era, but they have different urban spaces, museums and relationships with the volcanic landscape.

The 24-day journey includes León Viejo, modern León, Managua, [Masaya Volcano](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) and Granada. The history here includes eruptions that changed the location of settlements. The 26-day itinerary takes another order: after arriving in Managua, the group visits Granada and Masaya, then León and later [Estelí](/nicaragua/place/esteli/), with urban murals and a cigar factory visit. Estelí adds living crafts and modern city culture absent in quite the same form from the shorter programme.

Explore [Nicaragua's culture and history itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/nicaragua/) for a closer look at the country. City walks and a crater excursion have different purposes and access requirements. Check the current availability of the natural site for the selected dates.

## Panama: colonial architecture, the canal and Emberá culture

In [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), the itinerary combines old-city districts with the engineering history of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/). At [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/), the focus is on colonial streets and buildings. Miraflores has a different story: locks, passing ships and how the canal transformed the region's transport geography. These are two distinct sightseeing themes worth experiencing in one city.

Another important day is devoted to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and the village of [Tusipono](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/). Travelling along the river leads to encounters with Emberá crafts and traditions. The 24-day programme specifically mentions local handicrafts, dances and a traditional lunch. The 26-day programme schedules the Chagres and Tusipono excursion from 08:00 to 16:00. It is an opportunity to learn about living culture rather than reducing Panama to its canal and skyscrapers.

For more detailed options, browse [Panama cultural programmes](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/panama/). If time is limited, decide whether the historic district and canal or a full day in Chagres is more important. The longer itineraries considered here combine both experiences.

## Comparing the itineraries: 24 or 26 days

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days,tour_source_luchshee_v_tsentralnoj_amerike}}

The **24-day “Best of Central America”** starts in Guatemala and also travels through El Salvador and Costa Rica. After Nicaragua comes a Costa Rican nature section and then Panama with Boquete, Barú Volcano, the capital, Chagres and relaxation on the Pacific coast. This option particularly suits travellers seeking history alongside nature and beach days at the end.

The **26-day journey through eight countries** adds Mexico and Belize before Guatemala, and Estelí within Nicaragua. It includes a flight between El Salvador and Managua; later, the route continues through Costa Rica to Panama City. This option offers wider geography and historical context but needs closer attention to flight connections and the full journey's duration.

The three selected countries **are not consecutive uninterrupted sections**: El Salvador lies between Honduras and Nicaragua, and Costa Rica between Nicaragua and Panama. We help match the actual order with your available days, interests and transfer requirements. Shortening the tour to only these three countries would require a separately redesigned programme and must not be presented as an existing feature of either tour.

## Preparing for a historical journey

For Copán, comfortable shoes and time for outdoor archaeological sites are useful. Nicaraguan city walks may be combined with a volcanic visit, requiring clothes and a pace suited to both. In Panama, capital-city sightseeing and the Chagres excursion call for different preparation: more urban walking in the first case, and a river trip and time in nature in the second.

Visa and transit rules must be checked **for each traveller's nationality** and the full country sequence, including El Salvador and Costa Rica. Passport validity, health requirements and rules for re-entry at border crossings also matter. We can help plan the sequence and checks before flights are booked; specific requirements must be confirmed under current rules of each country.

## Frequently asked questions about the history of Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama

### Are all three countries included in a single ready-made tour?

Yes. Both itineraries include Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama as main countries. One lasts 24 days and covers six states; the other lasts 26 days and covers eight. These pages do not promise the same schedule for a three-country-only tour.

### What is the most important site in Honduras?

The main historical visit on these journeys is Copán, with carved stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. Other Honduran regions must not be assumed included.

### How are León and Granada different?

Both cities have colonial heritage. León offers more about the cathedral and urban arts; Granada features older districts and the architecture of a city by the lake. The 26-day programme adds Estelí.

### What should I choose in Panama: the canal or an Emberá village?

They tell different historical and cultural stories. The canal reveals the country's engineering and trade history, while Tusipono introduces a community's crafts and traditions. Both long tours include both themes, though their scheduling differs.

## Nature in Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama: what is actually included

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} listing all three as main destinations and tagged "Nature". The nature experiences, however, are unevenly distributed. Both tours visit the archaeological monuments of Copán in Honduras. Masaya Volcano is the principal natural attraction in Nicaragua. Panama offers either a mix of mountains, rivers and coast or a shorter excursion on the Chagres River.

These are not standalone three-country journeys: the [24-day “Best of Central America”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) covers six countries and the [26-day route](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) eight. Other stages of travel lie between Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama.

## Honduras: Copán is more about Maya heritage

Both itineraries visit [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) in Honduras. The ancient city stands in green surroundings, but its main attractions are archaeological structures, stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. **Neither itinerary includes a dedicated wildlife-watching programme or a trek through Honduran nature parks.**

This matters when choosing a trip for its natural attractions. If you particularly want Honduran rainforest, a reserve walk or a marine ecosystem, the actual content of the excursion days must be checked separately. The "Nature" tag on a large multi-country tour does not establish such activities in every country.

Honduras has its own appeal here: archaeology in tropical vegetation, contrasting with volcanic Nicaragua and river landscapes in Panama.

## Nicaragua: an active volcano and brief urban stops

After Honduras, the routes pass through El Salvador before reaching Nicaragua. The 24-day programme includes León Viejo, [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/), Managua, [Masaya](/nicaragua/place/masaya/) and [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/). The longer eight-country itinerary adds Estelí after Granada and León.

The main natural attraction is [Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/). An important distinction: the crater visit is scheduled alongside city sightseeing, not as a separate expedition lasting several days. Park access can be restricted depending on volcanic activity and safety rules; confirm arrangements before travelling.

For volcano enthusiasts, Nicaragua is a strong part of this combination, but the days available in the country also include museums, historic districts and transfers.

## Panama: why one itinerary offers more nature

On [“Best of Central America”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/), Panama begins around [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/). One day is set aside for [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/), followed by a flight from David to Panama City. After the urban section comes [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) with a visit to an Emberá community. The itinerary concludes with time on the Pacific coast.

These are three different nature experiences: mountain scenery, humid river forest and the coast. However, the specific conditions of the Barú excursion depend on weather and access; including a volcano in the schedule does not itself mean a challenging climb on foot.

On the [26-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), travellers fly from Costa Rica into Panama City. There is a day on the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/) and at the Emberá village of Tusipono, followed by the Miraflores Locks and city sightseeing. Boquete, Barú and beach days are not part of this programme.

**If Panama should be the nature-focused finale of the journey**, the 24-day itinerary offers more time and more varied landscapes. If the priority is exploring Central America on a wider route including Mexico and Belize, the 26-day tour serves a different purpose.

## How to distinguish the actual content of the programmes

| Traveller's goal | What the comparison shows |
|---|---|
| I want Masaya Volcano and Chagres | Both sites feature in both programmes |
| I also want Barú Volcano | Included in the 24-day itinerary |
| I want a nature day in Honduras | This requires separate agreement: Copán is an archaeological stop |
| I want to visit more countries | Eight on the 26-day tour versus six |

Some nature highlights of both tours take place in Costa Rica: the 24-day version includes Arenal, Monteverde, Caño Negro and Manuel Antonio; the 26-day version includes Arenal, Monteverde and Tortuguero. Do not attribute these places to the three countries in the filter. For the whole journey, see the [general Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama combination](/multi-country/honduras_nicaragua_panama/) or [multi-country nature tours](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Borders, safety and weather

Copán, Masaya and Chagres are far apart. Between them, the itineraries cross El Salvador and Costa Rica and, on some programmes, include flights. It would therefore be wrong to treat the trip as three consecutive excursions in neighbouring countries.

Volcanic areas and the Chagres River require access checks close to the departure date. In August 2026, Panama's environmental authorities temporarily closed Chagres Park because of rising water levels before reporting that visits could resume. This illustrates why river excursions and waterfall visits require separate confirmation. Also check entry rules for the traveller's nationality in **every country on the actual itinerary**, even when the filter contains only three.

Useful equipment includes shoes for volcanic terrain, rain protection and a waterproof bag for river excursions. The exact choice depends on whether the selected itinerary includes Barú and how access to it is arranged.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama

### Do these tours include a safari or wildlife watching in Honduras?

No separate safari is confirmed. Honduras is represented by archaeological Copán. Wildlife watching on the overall multi-country journey may take place elsewhere, chiefly in Costa Rica.

### Which programme visits Barú Volcano?

The [24-day “Best of Central America” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/). On the [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), the Panama section is limited to Panama City and Chagres.

### Should the Chagres excursion be confirmed in advance?

Yes. River levels and national park regulations can change the availability of the boat route and individual sections. The exact day's activities depend on current conditions.

## Where wildlife is watched on routes through these three countries

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} travelling through [Honduras](/honduras/), [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/) and [Panama](/panama/) and tagged "Wildlife and Safaris". Both routes include **several additional countries**. The theme applies to the whole tour; it does not mean that all three selected countries feature equal numbers of safaris, birdwatching outings or reserve excursions.

The actual programmes have the following distribution: visitors see [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) in Honduras, combine colonial cities with [Masaya Volcano](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) in Nicaragua and explore [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) in Panama. The 24-day itinerary adds the mountain scenery of [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) and the Boquete region.

**The main specialist tropical wildlife-watching experiences on these journeys occur in Costa Rica**, a subsequent stage outside the selected three. This distinction matters: bird and mammal enthusiasts should evaluate the entire itinerary, not assume the catalogue promises "safaris in three countries".

## Honduras: nature around Copán without an invented safari

Both tours stop at [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) for Maya sculptures and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. Tropical greenery and hills form the setting of the archaeological visit, but **the published programme includes no separately confirmed wildlife-watching day in Honduras**.

It makes sense to regard the Honduras section as a cultural encounter in a natural landscape: an ancient city amid greenery, a walking tour of the ruins and a transfer onwards. Anyone travelling specifically for forest birds or mammals should choose a programme with dedicated observation activities or discuss an addition. A country's presence in the general [Honduras nature travel catalogue](/interests/nature/tours/honduras/) does not confirm those activities on every listed itinerary.

## Nicaragua: Masaya Volcano and different landscapes

In [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/), the natural element is more pronounced. Both programmes name [Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/), alongside historic stops at [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/) and [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/). The principal nature experience here is volcanic terrain, not a search for wild animals.

On the [26-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), visitors reach Managua by air, then explore Granada and Masaya, followed by León and [Estelí](/nicaragua/place/esteli/). On the [24-day “Best of Central America”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/), the route continues through Managua to Masaya and Granada after visiting León. The balance of towns and volcanoes differs, but none of these stops automatically becomes an excursion to spot monkeys or rare birds.

Access to the crater and parts of the volcanic park depends on current activity and the decisions of the authorities. We help verify visiting conditions for the chosen dates; permanent unrestricted access to the crater cannot be promised.

## Panama: Chagres, a river ecosystem and Barú Volcano

In [Panama](/panama/), both itineraries feature a day on the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) visiting the Emberá village of [Tusipono](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/). It combines river scenery, a waterfall and cultural encounters. The 24-day description notes that capuchin monkeys may be seen in the area. This is a possibility, not a guaranteed service.

On the 26-day tour, the Chagres excursion is scheduled from 08:00 to 16:00. The river trip and natural conditions along the banks matter, but sightings of particular animal species are not among the guaranteed activities.

The 24-day itinerary additionally includes Boquete and [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). The programme specifies a 4×4 excursion on a mountain road. Its main appeal is the high-altitude landscape and, when the weather is clear, a panoramic view. It is not a specialist birdwatching excursion or jungle walk; conditions on the summit are cooler and very different from the humid Chagres valley.

Compare [Panama nature itineraries](/interests/nature/tours/panama/) by the Chagres experience, mountains and confirmed excursion days.

## Where more wildlife watching takes place on these same tours

Both programmes have a substantial Costa Rican section. The 24-day journey includes Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge, Monteverde cloud forest, the Tárcoles River with crocodiles and birds, and Manuel Antonio National Park. The 26-day journey names Monteverde, Arenal and a dawn boat trip along the Tortuguero canals. These days develop the nature theme much more fully than the stop at Copán.

Those destinations belong to [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and its [wildlife-watching programmes](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/). They should be considered when evaluating **the full trip**, but they are not visits within the three countries selected on this page. Travellers who want to focus on wildlife and reduce archaeology should choose based on these specific stages.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days,tour_source_luchshee_v_tsentralnoj_amerike}}

## Logistics and preparation for nature days

Honduran Copán, volcanic Nicaragua and Panama's humid regions call for different clothes and schedules. Comfortable shoes suit a day's archaeological sightseeing; volcano visits depend on up-to-date access restrictions; Chagres requires clothing and waterproof protection suitable for a river excursion. Barú demands warmer layers than low-lying coasts.

On the 24-day tour, these stages are separated by travel through El Salvador and Costa Rica; the 26-day option includes flights between countries. Actual time allowances follow the full itinerary, not the number of countries named in a filter. We help compare the stages and journey length before discussing possible reductions.

Any wildlife sighting depends on habitat and time of day. Even where an excursion is described as nature-focused, the species encountered cannot be guaranteed. This is true on Chagres as well as the specialist Costa Rican sections.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on journeys through Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama

### Can we see animals in all three countries on a single tour?

Tours covering all three countries exist, but their programmes do not include equivalent wildlife-watching excursions in each. Honduras centres on Copán, Nicaragua on Masaya Volcano and Panama on Chagres; observation activities are described in greatest detail on the Costa Rican stage.

### How do Panama's nature sections differ?

Chagres is a forested river environment with an excursion to an Emberá community. Barú Volcano is a mountain drive in a 4×4 vehicle, offered only on the 24-day tour. Choose between the landscapes and physical conditions; the outings are not interchangeable.

### Are sightings of capuchin monkeys on Chagres guaranteed?

No. One description mentions the possibility of seeing capuchins, but sightings depend on the animals and conditions. The confirmed activities are a river trip and a visit to Tusipono.

### How should we choose between 24 and 26 days?

The 24-day tour adds the Boquete highlands and Barú to Chagres, along with several major Costa Rican nature sites. The 26-day journey covers eight countries, including Mexico and Belize, and includes watching wildlife on the Tortuguero canals. The deciding factors are the full geography and actual nature days, not just the number of days.

## Honduras and Panama: from a Maya city to the Panama Canal

**The main reason to combine Honduras and Panama is the contrast between ancient Mesoamerican history and modern engineering.** Western [Honduras](/honduras/) is home to [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) and its Maya archaeological complex. In [Panama](/panama/), travellers visit [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), the [Panama Canal and Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/), and tropical forests.

The countries are not neighbours. An overland Central American itinerary typically passes through El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica between Honduras and Panama, with the actual order determined by the programme. Flights also have to be planned according to current schedules and possible connections.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Honduras and Panama as main countries. These are extended multi-country journeys. For a short trip visiting only Copán and Panama City, a separate custom itinerary would be needed; it must not be presented as already included.

## Two itineraries: different Panama experiences after Copán

| Programme | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Best of Central America, 24 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) | Copán, then Boquete, Barú and Panama's beaches |
| [Central America, 8 countries in 26 days](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) | Copán, more countries and a compact Panama finale |

On the [24-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/), Guatemala precedes Honduras. After [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/), the itinerary heads to Copán: arrival near the ruins is followed by sightseeing at the archaeological complex and a transfer to [San Salvador](/el-salvador/place/san-salvador/). Nicaragua and Costa Rica come next. Panama includes [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/), [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/), a David–Panama City flight, the canal, [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and free days on the Pacific coast at [Playa Blanca](/panama/place/playa-blanca/).

On the [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Copán comes later in the overall sequence, after Mexico, Belize and Guatemala. Travellers transfer from [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) to Copán, explore the ruins the next day and head to San Salvador. They reach Panama after Nicaragua and Costa Rica, flying from San José to Panama City. The final days include Chagres Park, an Emberá community, the capital and canal. **Boquete and beach days are not included in this programme.**

The first itinerary suits travellers wanting more time in mountains and by the ocean after visiting ancient cities. The second is designed for a broader journey across Central America, from Mexico to Panama. Compare specific overnight stays and transfers, not only the overall length.

## Copán: why the archaeological site deserves time

[Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) is one of the most important urban centres of Classic Maya civilisation. Its carved stone stelae, plazas and temples reveal the skill of sculptors and the complex history of local rulers. UNESCO has inscribed the complex on its World Heritage List.

The Hieroglyphic Stairway is especially significant because of its long sequence of inscriptions. Copán's stories involve dynasties and religious life in the ancient city. Both the monuments in the plaza and the architecture of the Acropolis reward attention. Conservation rules must be respected: some areas may be inaccessible, and the stairway is protected from damage.

Both published itineraries do include a visit to Copán, but their schedules are tight: the group stays overnight near the ruins on arrival, then moves onwards after the archaeological tour. Travellers interested in studying the site in greater detail should discuss extending their time at Copán instead of assuming any extra excursion will fit the standard day.

Logistics matter as well. [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) lies in western Honduras, not far from Guatemala. On both extended routes, Honduras is reached from Guatemala and followed by travel towards El Salvador. Road conditions, border formalities and departure times therefore affect the following day.

## Panama after Copán: capital, mountains or coast

[Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) tells a very different story. Its modern business districts, waterfront and historic quarters are visible side by side. At the [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/), visitors can watch ships passing and learn how the Panama Canal operates. After Copán's ancient temples, this is a tangible contrast between engineering achievements of different periods.

Both tours include a nature excursion to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/). It involves river travel and encounters with Emberá culture, including a visit to [Tusipono village](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/) on the relevant itinerary. Weather, river access and transport arrangements matter; this is a separate day trip beyond city sightseeing.

The 24-day trip has two additional Panama features. The first is the [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) highlands and an off-road outing to [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/), where conditions are cooler than in the capital. The second is time at [Playa Blanca](/panama/place/playa-blanca/) on the Pacific. These days may be decisive if you want to rest after intensive visits to ancient cities.

The 26-day programme's Panama section is a shorter finale. It covers the city, canal and Chagres, but does not list Playa Blanca or Barú. The distinction matters for both prices and the kind of journey offered; the same package of Panama services must not be attributed to both tours.

## Borders and entry: CA-4 in Honduras, separate arrangements in Panama

**Honduras is in CA-4; Panama is not.** The CA-4 agreement comprises Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua. For foreign tourists, an authorised period of stay may be shared across several countries in this area. Crossing from Guatemala into Honduras should therefore not be assumed to start a new, independent full period.

Both 24- and 26-day itineraries continue through other countries after Honduras. Check the order of border crossings, the date of first entry into CA-4 and the remaining permitted stay on departure. Costa Rica and Panama are outside this agreement and apply their own rules.

Visa requirements, passport validity, evidence of return or onward travel and proof of funds depend on **nationality and the type of travel document**. Rules for Russian citizens and travellers using other passports should be reviewed separately for each country on the itinerary. Transit states and re-entry after a connection or excursion must also be considered.

According to Panama's immigration authorities, tourists need valid documents, a visa where applicable, proof of departure and sufficient funds under the established rules. The information published by official immigration authorities was checked on **15 October 2026** and requires rechecking for each passport and route immediately before travel.

We help map out border crossings and coordinate documentation and transport connections, but the final decision on admission belongs to each country's immigration service.

## Lempiras in Honduras and dollars in Panama

Honduras uses the **lempira (HNL)** as its national currency. In Panama, the **US dollar** is widely used for daily tourist payments, while the balboa is the national monetary unit, including coins. Travelling from Honduras to Panama therefore involves changing the currency you use, even on one longer tour.

A 24- or 26-day trip also involves expenditure in other countries: Guatemala uses quetzals; Nicaragua and Costa Rica have their own currencies. One currency exchange before departure will not cover the entire itinerary conveniently. Separate included services from personal spending, tips, meals not covered by the programme and optional tickets.

Do not rely on Visa and Mastercard issued by Russian banks for international payments. Cards from foreign banks must be checked with the issuer and relevant payment network. With frequent transfers, a backup payment method and a reasonable amount of cash are useful, but avoid keeping all funds in one place.

Compare costs **against the actual itinerary**, including any separate terms for domestic flights and baggage. If one programme does not publish a price, it is not appropriate to invent a minimum.

## Weather and clothing: Copán is different from Chagres

Western Honduras around Copán differs in temperature and humidity from the Caribbean coast. Rainy periods and road conditions affect overland travel. A general guide to the relatively dry season is **November–April**, but the forecast for Copán itself matters for a particular date.

[Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) are warm and humid, whereas [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Barú](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) can be distinctly cooler. In much of central and Pacific Panama, the dry season usually falls in December–March. This overlap with drier weather in Honduras makes winter a useful option to consider, but it does not rule out rain in specific locations.

For Copán, pack comfortable closed shoes, water and sun protection. Chagres calls for quick-drying clothes, rain and insect protection. The Barú mountain section needs a warm layer, while the beach calls for lightweight clothes. Check baggage allowances for international and domestic flights: an extra suitcase complicates a journey crossing several borders.

Health requirements, insurance and possible yellow fever vaccination rules must be reviewed against **every country actually visited or transited**. The mention of Honduras and Panama in the title does not provide a complete answer for a long itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about a Honduras and Panama trip

### Can I visit just Honduras and Panama without other countries?

A custom trip involving flights can be planned separately. The existing programmes on this page are longer journeys through Central America in which the other countries are substantial stages.

### Which sights appear in both itineraries?

Both include [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), the canal and the Chagres nature area. Days, transport and additional stops differ.

### Which one includes Barú Volcano and a beach holiday?

The [24-day “Best of Central America” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) includes Boquete, Barú and Playa Blanca. The [26-day programme](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) ends with sightseeing around the capital and Chagres.

### Is there one visa covering both Honduras and Panama?

There is no single visa automatically permitting entry into both countries. Honduras belongs to CA-4; Panama does not. Visa conditions and length of stay depend on citizenship and need separate confirmation.

### Which currency should I use in each country?

The main currency in Honduras is the lempira, while US dollars are widely used in Panama. A multi-country itinerary requires payment arrangements for the intermediate countries too.

### Should I travel in winter or summer?

For many stops, roughly December to March is convenient. The route nevertheless spans mountains, forest and ocean, so weather should be assessed by region and date. Whether archaeology, nature or beaches matter most also affects the choice of season.

## Honduras: Copán and a walk through the ancient city

The Honduras section focuses on [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). After arrival and an overnight stay near Copán Ruinas, travellers explore the archaeological complex: carved stelae, plazas and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. Copán was a major centre of Maya civilisation, known for stone sculpture and hieroglyphic inscriptions. The archaeological site is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

**Walking through Copán requires time outdoors and movement between ancient structures.** This is a cultural and historical visit, not a promised challenging trek or rafting excursion. Activities offered later in other countries must not be attributed to Honduras simply because the overall journey has an "Adventure" tag.

The Honduras section lies between [Lake Atitlán and Guatemala's volcanic landscapes](/guatemala/) and the archaeological sites of El Salvador. The programme separates arrival at Copán from the following day's exploration of the ruins and onward journey, leaving time to recover after the drive.

## Panama: the Chagres River, a waterfall and an Emberá settlement

The Panama section begins after several nature days in Costa Rica. First, the group flies from San José to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). Travellers then visit [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/), where the river and dense tropical forest shape the day.

Our Chagres excursion runs **from 08:00 to 16:00**. It includes a journey on the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/), swimming near a waterfall and a visit to the [Emberá village of Tusipono](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/). The village visit includes a traditional lunch, music, dances and local crafts. Panama's tourism authority also describes Tusipono and other Emberá communities as destinations on river excursions.

**The river section is a sightseeing boat excursion, not an advertised white-water rafting trip.** Water, slippery ground near the waterfall, heat and humidity require appropriate shoes and protection for your belongings. Boat operations and waterfall access depend on weather and actual conditions.

The final day covers the [Panama Canal and city](/panama/place/panama-city/): the Miraflores Locks, historic districts and the Amador Causeway. The sightseeing lasts 6 hours, followed by an airport transfer. The departure flight must be coordinated with the day's duration.
